pages.text: An airlock spends real oxygen every cycle. The controller keeps a reserve.

pages.title: Units
pages.text: Each interior block holds $(bold)100$() O2 units; the reserve holds $(bold)6,400$().$(br2)Units match canisters, ten per player-second. They aren't liters.

pages.title: Refilling
pages.text: A breathable base with a Geothermal Core refills the reserve at up to $(bold)40 units/s$(), from spare production only.
Breathing and flames come first; reservoirs, Core canisters and EVA refill share the rest fairly.$(br2)Stored O2 works without the Core. A charged O2 canister supplies backup gas.

pages.title: Cycle Costs
pages.text: Pressurizing spends the chamber's fill. Depressurizing recovers $(bold)90%$(); 10% vents.$(br2)Anything past a full reserve is lost.

pages.title: Canisters
pages.text: Use an O2 canister on a panel to transfer what fits. The rest stays in the canister.

pages.title: Recovery
pages.text: The Core can't refill an evacuated airlock; cycle the controller.$(br2)Reserve and partial transfers survive reloads. Unloaded chambers pause; they don't load chunks.

pages.title: Repairs
pages.text: $(danger)Breaking the last panel loses its reserve.$() Rebuilding or resizing creates no free air and may lose it.$(br2)Relight torches only after pressure returns. No power grid needed.
